text: The normal readings from your neck X-ray are helpful, but they do not rule out soft tissue or neurological issues causing your symptoms. To better understand the pattern of your pain and weakness, please tell me if your arm paresthesias follow a specific nerve path (like shooting down the thumb or pinky) and whether your weakness affects your grip strength. speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive bilateral hand weakness in a 58-year-old male with diabetes is highly concerning for cervical radiculopathy or myelopathy, possibly complicated by diabetic neuropathy. Since your X-ray was normal, the MRI results I requested will be crucial to see if there is spinal cord compression or a disc herniation. Have you noticed any loss of sensation in your legs, balance issues, or changes in bladder control?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of burning pain, paresthesias, bilateral hand weakness, absent reflexes, and fasciculations in a patient with diabetes is highly suggestive of a specific neurological condition affecting the lower cervical cord. Given your history of diabetes and hypertension, could you confirm if you have noticed any recent issues with bladder control or significant difficulty walking? REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI. DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)
